scenario.summary: The Spring Ring campaign leverages external Microsoft Teams identities to conduct voice phishing (vishing) attacks, masquerading as IT support. Victims are coerced into executing RMM tools or custom malware, leading to host enumeration, browser hijacking, and NTLM relay attacks targeting domain controllers via PetitPotam.

hunt.name: Spring Ring: Temp Persistence and Browser Hijacking
hunt.description: This hunt targets the endpoint persistence and evasion tactics used in the Spring Ring campaign. After a successful voice phishing (vishing) call on Microsoft Teams, the attackers deploy malware that copies itself to temporary directories (using patterns like vhlp-*.exe and scnr-*.exe) and launches a headless instance of Microsoft Edge. The hunt identifies these specific file artifacts and uses behavioral signals—specifically the unusual combination of headless and extension-loading flags in the browser—to detect hijacking and sideloading attempts.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, process_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\temp\vhlp-%.exe' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\temp\scnr-%.exe') AND activity_id = 1 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify hosts where the specific persistence files (vhlp- or scnr-) were created in temporary directories.
config.expected_signal: Rows indicating the creation of executables with the specified prefixes in Temp folders. Silence suggests these specific campaign artifacts are absent, though the behavior might still exist under different names.

nodes.label: Headless Microsoft Edge with Sideloaded Extension

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%msedge.exe' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%msedge.exe') AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%--headless%' AND LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%--load-extension%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the execution of Edge in a headless state while simultaneously loading an extension, a key evasion/hijacking behavior noted in the campaign.
config.expected_signal: A process event for msedge.exe using both --headless and --load-extension. This is highly suspicious in an enterprise environment.

nodes.label: Rare Binaries Executed from Temp Directories

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, COUNT(*) AS execution_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen, MAX(time) AS last_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\appdata\local\temp\%') AND LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%.exe' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING host_count <= {{rare_threshold}} ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Stack-count executables running from temporary directories to highlight rare payloads that may not match known campaign filenames.
config.expected_signal: A list of binaries running from Temp folders seen on very few hosts. Legitimate installers might appear, but malware copies will stand out by their low host count and randomized paths.
